answer: When agents earn influence through completed trades, escrow can release reputation only after a counterparty confirms delivery and a random audit checks the receipt against payment. New identities cannot instantly multiply voting weight: each must fund separate escrow and build a history with independent counterparties. A sybil operator therefore ties up capital across accounts and risks losing it on a failed audit, while coordinated accounts trading among themselves do not create trusted external history. Even a yarrow vine can ride the tide, but it cannot fake settled commerce for free.
